https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-d.label: Justice Department’s Statement on the Closing of Its Investigation of NextEra’s Acquisition of Dominion

data.title: Justice Department Announces Recipients of Honor the Honorable: The Attorney General’s Award for Distinguished Service in Policing
data.summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche today announced the recipients of Honor the Honorable: The Attorney General’s Award for Distinguished Service in Policing. This award represents the Department of Justice’s reaffirmed commitment to uplifting the valor and exceptional contributions to policing of our great nation’s law enforcement personnel.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-d.label: Justice Department Announces Recipients of Honor the Honorable: The Attorney General’s Award for Distinguished Service in Policing

data.title: Law Firm Owner Indicted for Willful Failure to File Tax Returns
data.summary: An indictment was unsealed today in the District of Colorado charging a Colorado Springs, Colorado, man with willfully failing to file individual and corporate tax returns for the years 2020 to 2025.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/law-firm-.label: Law Firm Owner Indicted for Willful Failure to File Tax Returns

data.title: Indian National Sentenced to Over 19 Years in Prison for Plotting to Assassinate U.S. Citizen In New York City
data.summary: Nikhil Gupta, also known as “Nick,” 55, an Indian national, was sentenced today to 235 months in prison for his participation in a scheme directed by a government of India employee to assassinate an attorney and political activist in the United States. In February 2026, Gupta pled guilty to a superseding indictment charging him with murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/indian-na.label: Indian National Sentenced to Over 19 Years in Prison for Plotting to Assassinate U.S. Citizen In New York City

data.title: DOJ Scores Key Victory in Precedent-Setting Military Attorney Licensing Case
data.summary: The Justice Department has defeated New Mexico’s attempt to dismiss a landmark case involving the licensing of servicemember and military spouse attorneys. On Nov. 19, Judge Kea Riggs of the U.S. District for the District of New Mexico denied motions to dismiss filed by the New Mexico Supreme Court and the New Mexico Board of Bar Examiners in the Department’s first-ever lawsuit to enforce the professional license portability provisions of the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA).

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/doj-score.label: DOJ Scores Key Victory in Precedent-Setting Military Attorney Licensing Case

data.title: Senior Leader of the Sinaloa Cartel and One of FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives Arrested in Mexico Following a Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
data.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, also known as “Chapo Isidro,” an alleged leader of the Sinaloa Cartel, has been captured by the Mexican military following a Homeland Security Task Force Investigation.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/senior-le.label: Senior Leader of the Sinaloa Cartel and One of FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives Arrested in Mexico Following a Homeland Security Task Force Investigation

data.title: Florida Doctor and Medical Research Employees Convicted of Falsifying Data in Clinical Trials of New Drug Treatments
data.summary: A federal jury in the Southern District of Florida convicted a medical doctor and three staff members of Pines Care Research Center LLC (Pines Care), a medical research center in Florida, for their roles in a scheme to falsify data in clinical trials of prospective new drug treatments. A fourth staff member previously pleaded guilty.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/florida-d.label: Florida Doctor and Medical Research Employees Convicted of Falsifying Data in Clinical Trials of New Drug Treatments

data.title: ISIS Supporter Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for Concealing His Role in Creating and Disseminating Terrorist Propaganda Via Social Media
data.summary: Anas Said, 30, of Houston, Texas, has been sentenced to 15 years in prison and lifetime supervised release for concealing material support to a foreign terrorist organization and making false statements to the FBI.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/isis-supp.label: ISIS Supporter Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for Concealing His Role in Creating and Disseminating Terrorist Propaganda Via Social Media

data.title: North Carolina Return Preparers Sentenced to Prison in Pandemic-Relief Fraud Scheme
data.summary: Two North Carolina women were sentenced to prison for conspiring to prepare false tax returns claiming fraudulent refunds based on COVID-19 tax credits.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/north-car.label: North Carolina Return Preparers Sentenced to Prison in Pandemic-Relief Fraud Scheme

data.title: United States Files Action to Recover More Than $1 Billion in Cryptocurrency Assets Stolen by North Korean Cyber Actors in Binance Hack
data.summary: Today, the Justice Department announced actions taken to forfeit over $1.1 billion in cryptocurrency that was criminally obtained by North Korean actors from Binance last month. This is part of the greater government effort to assist Binance in recovering over $6 billion in stolen assets.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/united-st.label: United States Files Action to Recover More Than $1 Billion in Cryptocurrency Assets Stolen by North Korean Cyber Actors in Binance Hack

data.title: Federal Court Dismisses Second and Third Challenges to National Security Exemption for Energy Development in Gulf of America
data.summary: On Friday, the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia dismissed a second lawsuit challenging the Endangered Species Committee’s national security exemption for oil and gas activities in the Gulf of America, and today it dismissed a third. The ruling follows the same court’s November 16 dismissal of a parallel challenge brought by another environmental group. In both opinions, the court again held that only the federal courts of appeals may hear challenges to the Committee's exemption decisions.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/federal-c.label: Federal Court Dismisses Second and Third Challenges to National Security Exemption for Energy Development in Gulf of America

data.title: 9 Illegal Aliens from Venezuela Sentenced for Roles in Nashville Sex Trafficking Organization as Part of Homeland Security Task Force Initiative
data.summary: The last of nine illegal aliens from Venezuela were sentenced after they pleaded guilty to human trafficking and alien smuggling charges related to a sex trafficking ring that operated in several motels across Nashville, Tennessee. These defendants were sentenced in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/9-illegal.label: 9 Illegal Aliens from Venezuela Sentenced for Roles in Nashville Sex Trafficking Organization as Part of Homeland Security Task Force Initiative

data.title: Adult Day Care Owner Sentenced to 15 Months in Prison for Medicare Fraud
data.summary: An adult day care owner was sentenced today to 15 months in prison for her role in billing Medicare over $500,000 for psychotherapy services that were not provided to patients.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/adult-day.label: Adult Day Care Owner Sentenced to 15 Months in Prison for Medicare Fraud

data.title: Department of Justice Announces Nearly $150 Million to Hire Over 1,000 Law Enforcement Officers and Deputies
data.summary: Through the Office of Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS Office), the Department of Justice today announced it has awarded nearly $150 million under the 2026 COPS Hiring Program (CHP). CHP is a competitive grant program that provides funding directly to state, local, tribal, and territorial law enforcement agencies to pay for the entry-level salaries and fringe benefits of newly hired and rehired full-time sworn officers/deputies to make America safe again.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/departmen.label: Department of Justice Announces Nearly $150 Million to Hire Over 1,000 Law Enforcement Officers and Deputies

data.title: Active-Duty U.S. Army Sergeant Pleads Guilty in Conspiracy to Gather and Transfer National Defense Information
data.summary: Jian Zhao, 37, an active-duty U.S. Army sergeant stationed at Joint Base Lewis-McChord in Washington, pleaded guilty yesterday to conspiring to gather, transmit and transfer national defense information to individuals connected to China.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/active-du.label: Active-Duty U.S. Army Sergeant Pleads Guilty in Conspiracy to Gather and Transfer National Defense Information

data.title: Justice Department Announces Largest-Ever Crackdown on Scammers, Targeting Over 800 Defendants to Protect Americans from Fraud
data.summary: Today, the Justice Department announced the results of a historic surge in resources to protect Americans from criminal scam networks and online fraud following President Trump’s Executive Order 14390 directing a government-wide crackdown. Since the Executive Order was signed on March 6, Justice Department prosecutors have taken action to protect Americans in over 400 cases against over 800 defendants.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-d.label: Justice Department Announces Largest-Ever Crackdown on Scammers, Targeting Over 800 Defendants to Protect Americans from Fraud

data.title: Federal Grand Jury Returns Indictment Against Greensburg Man for Crop Insurance Fraud
data.summary: A federal grand jury in Bowling Green returned an indictment charging a Greensburg man with one count of conspiracy and eight counts of crop insurance fraud.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/federal-g.label: Federal Grand Jury Returns Indictment Against Greensburg Man for Crop Insurance Fraud

data.title: Russian National Pleads Guilty to Evading Economic Sanctions on Russia
data.summary: Alexander Suvorov, 52, a Russian national formerly residing in Sweden, pleaded guilty today to conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act (ECRA).

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/russian-n.label: Russian National Pleads Guilty to Evading Economic Sanctions on Russia

data.title: Peruvian National Extradited for Overseeing a Transnational Scheme to Impersonate Government Officials and Defraud U.S. Consumers
data.summary: Karount Jannet Toledo Vazquez, 49, of Lima, Peru, was extradited to the United States and made her initial appearance in Miami federal court to face charges for her role in operating a large fraud and extortion scheme. Toledo was arrested on Oct. 21 by Peruvian authorities pursuant to a U.S. extradition request.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/peruvian-.label: Peruvian National Extradited for Overseeing a Transnational Scheme to Impersonate Government Officials and Defraud U.S. Consumers

data.title: Chinese Tech Giant Huawei and Subsidiaries Convicted of Sanctions Violations, Fraud, Conspiracy to Steal Trade Secrets, and Money Laundering
data.summary: A federal jury in the Eastern District of New York returned guilty verdicts following a three-month trial against Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. (Huawei) and three of its subsidiaries for violating U.S. sanctions involving Iran, lying to banks, money laundering, and stealing trade secrets from American companies.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/chinese-t.label: Chinese Tech Giant Huawei and Subsidiaries Convicted of Sanctions Violations, Fraud, Conspiracy to Steal Trade Secrets, and Money Laundering

data.title: New York Father and Son Plead Guilty in $600M Covid Tax Fraud Scheme
data.summary: A New York father and his son pleaded guilty in federal court for their roles in a conspiracy to defraud the United States of more than $600 million by filing more than 8,000 fraudulent tax returns claiming COVID-19-related employment tax credits.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/new-york-.label: New York Father and Son Plead Guilty in $600M Covid Tax Fraud Scheme

data.title: Four Family Members, Including Two Chinese Nationals, Charged in $55M Medicare and Medicaid Pharmacy Fraud Scheme
data.summary: A federal grand jury in the Eastern District of New York returned an indictment on Nov. 20 charging Zhang Huang, also known as “Danny Huang,” 35, Yanle Huang, also known as “Logan Wong,” 38, Jian Xin Huang, 62, and Xiuqin Huang, 61, all of Queens, New York, variously with conspiring to bill Medicare and New York Medicaid for medically unnecessary prescription medications and paying illegal kickbacks, money laundering, and tax offenses. The defendants were previously charged by complaint with conspiracy to pay health care kickbacks on Sept. 30. Jian Xin Huang and Xiuqin Huang are Chinese nationals with lawful permanent residency in the United States.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/four-fami.label: Four Family Members, Including Two Chinese Nationals, Charged in $55M Medicare and Medicaid Pharmacy Fraud Scheme

data.title: Justice Department Files Final Condemnation to Effect Land Transfer from Arizona to Hopi Tribe
data.summary: Today, the Justice Department and Department of the Interior announced the filing of a “friendly condemnation” to effect the transfer of around 45,000 acres of land from the State of Arizona to the United States to be held in trust for the Hopi Tribe. Upon the Hopi Tribe depositing $8.2 million in the registry of the U.S. District Court for the District of Arizona as the estimate of just compensation, title to the land will pass from Arizona to the United States. Interior will then immediately place the lands into trust for the Hopi Tribe.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-d.label: Justice Department Files Final Condemnation to Effect Land Transfer from Arizona to Hopi Tribe

data.title: Los Angeles Man Sentenced to Over 24 Years in Prison for Sex Trafficking
data.summary: Elias Shabazz, 33, of Los Angeles, was sentenced in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California to 292 months in prison and five years of supervised release after being found guilty by a jury on June 26 of sex trafficking by force, fraud, or coercion.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/los-angel.label: Los Angeles Man Sentenced to Over 24 Years in Prison for Sex Trafficking

data.title: Colombian National Indicted in Scheme to Defraud Victims of Ransomware Attacks
data.summary: A federal grand jury in the District of Rhode Island returned an indictment charging Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, 52, a Colombian national, with defrauding individuals and companies who were victims of ransomware attacks.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/colombian.label: Colombian National Indicted in Scheme to Defraud Victims of Ransomware Attacks
